codeReview.summary: I reviewed the mission context, the e04f45b3-4acd-4333-9054-70203b701dc1 transcript skeleton, the handoff for commit 1c80bd5, and the feature footprint from commits ac8ea92 and 1c80bd5. The error envelope/sanitization work is substantial, but the feature still does not fully satisfy the wrong-method requirements in VAL-BH-006 because multiple GET-only handlers continue to accept unsupported methods or return the wrong status.

issues.description: Several read-only handlers in this file never validate `r.Method`: `TelemetryRoute` (line 22), `TelemetryStreamRoute` (line 54), `AdminOverviewRoute` (line 65), `AdminTelemetryRoute` (line 74), `EventsRoute` (line 87), and `EventsStreamRoute` (line 96). For an authenticated caller, unsupported methods like POST/DELETE still return 200 or open an SSE stream instead of a 405 `method_not_allowed` response, so the feature does not yet meet the
requirement in the feature description / VAL-BH-006.

Method handling is still incorrect on multiple supporting API routes. `TemplatesRoute` (line 34), `BackendResourcesRoute` (line 43), and `LogsRoute` (line 52) always return 200 for authenticated requests regardless of HTTP method, and `GitProvidersRoute` (line 61) returns 501 `not_implemented` for non-GET requests instead of 405 `method_not_allowed`. These endpoints therefore still violate the feature's required method-status semantics.

The new wrong-method coverage only exercises `Healthz`, `APIFallback`, `DeploymentsRoute`, `ProjectsRoute`, and `RepoImport` (see tests starting at lines 167, 229, 249, and 268). None of the unguarded telemetry/admin/event/misc routes are covered, which is why the incomplete 405 handling escaped despite the added test suite.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared guidance says to use structured errors and proper HTTP status codes, but it does not explicitly call out a route-level convention to use `requireMethod` (or otherwise reject unsupported methods) on every read-only handler. That gap likely contributed to the feature missing several GET-only routes.

summary: The feature meaningfully improves error normalization, sanitization, and error wrapping, but it is not complete: multiple GET-only API handlers still return 200/SSE (or 501) for unsupported methods instead of 405. I marked the review as failed until those route-level method checks are completed and covered by tests.
